sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Prevent malformed ice-class values from taking the non-applicable branch. On the top-level nltl:iceClass property constraint, require an IRI from the supplied controlled set (iceClassIaSuper, iceClassIa, iceClassIb, iceClassIc, iceClassIi, iceClassIii), e.g. with sh:nodeKind sh:IRI and sh:in. Keep the applicability branch restricted to IA Super or IA and retain the pre-2003-09-01 date test.

rows: Refactor the large Cartesian-product SPARQL constraint into conditional SHACL Core property/node constraints for each coefficient and L/T/B/clamped quantity: require the applicable properties, QuantityValue type, exactly one xsd:decimal numeric value, the prescribed unit, and the fixed coefficient value. Enforce constructionStageDate with SHACL Core sh:datatype xsd:date so an ill-formed xsd:date lexical form cannot bypass both queries; retain applicability as IA/IA Super with a date strictly before 2003-09-01. Keep only one bounded SPARQL constraint for ((L*T)/B^2)^3 and its [5,20] clamp, comparing the derived decimal with a tolerance rather than exact equality.

Bound the validation to avoid accidental passes and a combinatorial formula query: require exactly one value for each coefficient, shipLength, iceClassDraught, shipBreadth, and clampedHullGeometryTerm, and exactly one qudt:numericValue and qudt:unit on every quantity node. Add positive-value constraints, especially shipBreadth > 0, so division errors cannot suppress the SPARQL violation. Also add readiness constraints requiring exactly one constructionStageDate and iceClass for each assessed ship; otherwise missing applicability evidence currently causes the ship to escape the conditional target and pass.

Prevent malformed ice-class values from taking the non-applicable branch. On the top-level nltl:iceClass property constraint, require an IRI from the supplied controlled set (iceClassIaSuper, iceClassIa, iceClassIb, iceClassIc, iceClassIi, iceClassIii), e.g. with sh:nodeKind sh:IRI and sh:in. Keep the applicability branch restricted to IA Super or IA and retain the pre-2003-09-01 date test.
